stories.headline: Meta delays flagship AI model 'Avocado' to May after it underperforms vs Gemini and Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Meta postponed the release of its AI model codenamed 'Avocado' from March to at least May 2026, after internal tests showed it lagging behind newer models from Google and Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has postponed the release of its artificial intelligence model 'Avocado' to at least May, from this month, the New York Times reported on Thursday, citing sources.

key_facts.fact: Avocado's performance falls between Google's Gemini 2.5 and the latest Gemini 3.0 — it outperformed earlier Gemini versions and Meta's own prior models, but did not match the capabilities of the latest Gemini release or Anthropic's systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Internal tests showed 'Avocado' is lagging behind newer models from companies such as Alphabet Inc.'s Google and Anthropic. While Avocado performed better than Meta's earlier AI systems and even surpassed an earlier version of Google's Gemini model, it reportedly did not match the capabilities of the latest Gemini release.

key_facts.fact: Meta executives discussed the possibility of temporarily licensing technology from Google's Gemini models to support certain AI products while Avocado catches up, though no final decision was made.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta executives discussed the possibility of temporarily licensing technology from Google's Gemini models to support certain AI products, though no final decision was made.

key_facts.fact: The delay comes despite Meta projecting spending up to $135 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, nearly double the approximately $72 billion spent in 2025. Meta shares fell 2.55% on the news.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta projected spending up to $135 billion on AI infrastructure and capabilities in 2026, nearly double the approximately $72 billion spent in 2025. Meta shares fell 2.55% to $638.18.

key_facts.fact: Internally, Meta's focus is shifting toward a larger next-generation model codenamed 'Watermelon,' while a separate model called 'Mango' focuses on image and video generation.
key_facts.excerpt: Related Projects: Mango: A model focused on image and video generation. Watermelon: A future system in development.

stories.headline: NVIDIA AI-Q agent takes first place on both DeepResearch Bench I and II with open stack

key_facts.fact: NVIDIA's AI-Q deep research agent achieved first place on both DeepResearch Bench (55.95) and DeepResearch Bench II (54.50), the two primary benchmarks for evaluating deep research agents, using a single configurable open stack.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA AI-Q deep research agent recently achieved first place on both DeepResearch Bench(55.95) and DeepResearch Bench II(54.50), the two primary benchmarks for evaluating deep research agents.

key_facts.fact: AI-Q uses a three-component multi-agent architecture — orchestrator, planner, and researcher — with the researcher dispatching parallel specialists including Evidence Gatherer, Mechanism Explorer, Comparator, Critic, and Horizon Scanner.
key_facts.excerpt: Three-component system: Orchestrator coordinates the research loop, Planner maps information landscape and designs evidence-grounded research plans, Researcher dispatches parallel specialists (Evidence Gatherer, Mechanism Explorer, Comparator, Critic, Horizon Scanner).

key_facts.fact: The system runs on a fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B model, trained on 67,000 supervised fine-tuning trajectories that included real web search results, requiring approximately 25 hours on 16x8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: Fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B. 67,000 SFT trajectories filtered from ~80k generated. Training: 1 epoch, 5,615 steps, ~25 hours on 16×8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Winning both benchmarks is significant because they test complementary skills: DeepResearch Bench evaluates polished synthesis and narrative quality, while Bench II uses 70+ fine-grained binary rubrics verifying factual correctness and analytical rigor.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepResearch Bench tests polished, well-structured narratives and strong synthesis. DeepResearch Bench II uses 70+ fine-grained binary rubrics to verify granular factual correctness and analytical rigor.

key_facts.fact: The entire stack is open and config-driven — all components (LLMs, tools, graphs) are swappable via YAML, built on NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit and LangChain DeepAgents.
key_facts.excerpt: One configurable stack leading on both shows that developer accessible models and tooling can power state-of-the-art agentic research. All components (LLMs, tools, graphs) are swappable via YAML.

sources.title: How NVIDIA AI-Q Reached #1 on DeepResearch Bench I and II

stories.headline: Axiom raises $200M at $1.6B valuation to build formally verified AI-generated code

key_facts.fact: Axiom Quant raised a $200 million Series A led by Menlo Ventures, reaching a $1.6 billion valuation, following a $64 million seed round in October 2025. The company aims to eliminate AI hallucinations through formal mathematical verification.
key_facts.excerpt: The Series A round, which brings Axiom's valuation to $1.6 billion, was led by Menlo Ventures and represents a bet on a new paradigm it calls 'verified AI' that aims to eliminate the risk of 'hallucinations' once and for all.

key_facts.fact: Axiom trains AI systems to generate formally verified code outputs using Lean, a programming language for mathematical proofs, with deterministic proof verifiers ensuring each reasoning step is machine-checkable and logically guaranteed.
key_facts.excerpt: The technology uses 'deterministic proof verifiers' to ensure each step of reasoning is 'machine-checkable' and logically guaranteed. This provides mathematical certainty that AI-generated functions return correct answers.

key_facts.fact: The company creates a 'verified data flywheel' where proof-checked data feeds back into training loops, enabling recursive self-improvement without model collapse — each generation's outputs are formally verified before becoming the next generation's training data.
key_facts.excerpt: Axiom creates a 'verified data flywheel' of proof-checked data fed back into training loops, enabling recursive self-improvement without model collapse.

key_facts.fact: Axiom achieved a perfect score on the Putnam Competition (the world's hardest undergraduate math exam) in December 2025 and proved a 20-year-old number theory conjecture involving differential geometry.
key_facts.excerpt: December 2025: Perfect score on Putnam Competition (world's hardest undergraduate math exam). Proved a 20-year-old number theory conjecture involving differential geometry.

key_facts.fact: CEO Carina Hong is a 25-year-old Stanford Ph.D. student and MIT graduate. Co-founder Ken Ono is a Guggenheim/Packard/Sloan Fellow mathematician, and CTO Shubho Sengupta was formerly Facebook AI Research Director.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO: Carina Hong, 25-year-old Stanford Ph.D. student and MIT graduate. Mathematician Ken Ono (co-founder), Guggenheim/Packard/Sloan Fellow. CTO: Shubho Sengupta, former Facebook AI Research Director.

stories.headline: Microsoft open-sources AgentRx framework for systematically debugging AI agent failures

key_facts.fact: Microsoft Research published AgentRx on March 12, an automated debugging framework that pinpoints the 'critical failure step' in AI agent execution trajectories by synthesizing executable constraints from tool schemas and domain policies.
key_facts.excerpt: AgentRx pinpoints the first unrecoverable ('critical failure') step by synthesizing guarded, executable constraints from tool schemas and domain policies, then logging evidence-backed violations step-by-step.

key_facts.fact: AgentRx improved failure localization accuracy by 23.6% and root-cause attribution by 22.9% compared to prompting baselines across three agent benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: Results + release: AgentRx improves failure localization (+23.6%) and root-cause attribution (+22.9%) over prompting baselines.

key_facts.fact: The team released the AgentRx Benchmark with 115 manually annotated failed trajectories across three domains: tau-bench (structured API workflows), Flash (incident management), and Magentic-One (web and file tasks using multi-agent systems).
key_facts.excerpt: Benchmark + taxonomy: We release AgentRx Benchmark with 115 manually annotated failed trajectories across τ-bench, Flash, and Magentic-One, plus a grounded nine-category failure taxonomy.

key_facts.fact: The framework introduces a nine-category failure taxonomy covering issues like 'Plan Adherence Failure,' 'Invention of New Information,' and 'Invalid Invocation,' and the full framework, code, and dataset are open-sourced.
key_facts.excerpt: We release AgentRx Benchmark with 115 manually annotated failed trajectories across τ-bench, Flash, and Magentic-One, plus a grounded nine-category failure taxonomy. The framework and dataset are publicly available.

sources.title: Systematic debugging for AI agents: Introducing the AgentRx framework

stories.headline: Nature Medicine study: AI with cognitive layer outperforms human therapists on CBT in double-blind trial

key_facts.fact: A randomized, double-blind study published in Nature Medicine on March 12 found that LLMs augmented with Limbic's cognitive layer architecture consistently outperformed both standalone state-of-the-art LLMs and human clinicians across key competencies for delivering cognitive-behavioral therapy.
key_facts.excerpt: Randomized, double-blind trial shows Limbic's clinical reasoning layer turns leading LLMs into mental health specialists, achieving gold-standard clinical performance.

key_facts.fact: The trial involved 227 human participants generating naturalistic therapy session transcripts by interacting with different therapy agents, assessed by a consortium of 22 expert clinicians.
key_facts.excerpt: In a randomized, double-blind evaluation, 227 human participants generated naturalistic mental well-being session transcripts by interacting with different therapy agents. A consortium of 22 expert clinicians assessed these transcripts.

key_facts.fact: Results were validated on 19,674 transcripts from a large-scale real-world deployment supporting 8,920 users seeking mental well-being assistance. Increased cognitive layer activation was associated with greater symptom improvement and higher likelihood of long-term clinical recovery at approximately 10 weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: We validated these results in an analysis of 19,674 transcripts from a large-scale, real-world deployment where an LLM embedded within this cognitive layer architecture was used as part of healthcare delivery to support 8,920 users. Increased cognitive layer activation was associated with greater symptom improvement and a higher likelihood of long-term clinical recovery (~10 weeks).

key_facts.fact: Limbic CEO Ross Harper stated: 'Millions of people are already turning to general-purpose AI tools for mental health support, often without clinical validation or safeguards. Our study shows that safe, high-quality AI-enabled therapy is not just possible, but scientifically demonstrable.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Millions of people are already turning to general-purpose AI tools for mental health support, often without clinical validation or safeguards. Our study shows that safe, high-quality AI-enabled therapy is not just possible, but scientifically demonstrable.'

stories.headline: Databricks launches autonomous coding agent Genie Code and acquires Quotient AI

key_facts.fact: Databricks launched Genie Code, an autonomous AI agent for data engineering, data science, and analytics that can build pipelines, debug failures, ship dashboards, and maintain production systems end-to-end.
key_facts.excerpt: Databricks today launched Genie Code, an autonomous AI agent that fundamentally changes how data work gets done. Genie Code can carry out complex tasks such as building pipelines, debugging failures, shipping dashboards, and maintaining production systems.

key_facts.fact: On real-world data science tasks, Genie Code achieved a 77.1% success rate, more than doubling the 32.1% achieved by leading coding agents.
key_facts.excerpt: On real-world data science tasks, Databricks found Genie Code more than doubled the success rate of leading coding agents.

key_facts.fact: Databricks simultaneously acquired Quotient AI, an agent evaluation specialist whose founders previously led quality efforts for GitHub Copilot. Quotient monitors agent performance, catches regressions, and feeds a reinforcement learning loop.
key_facts.excerpt: Databricks acquired Quotient AI to strengthen continuous evaluation. Quotient monitors agent performance, measures answer quality, catches regressions, and feeds a reinforcement learning loop. Quotient's founders previously led quality efforts for GitHub Copilot.

key_facts.fact: CEO Ali Ghodsi stated: 'We are calling this Agentic Data Work. It will fundamentally change how enterprises make decisions,' emphasizing the shift from AI-assisted work to AI-driven work guided by humans.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO Ali Ghodsi stated: 'We are calling this Agentic Data Work. It will fundamentally change how enterprises make decisions.'

stories.headline: Gumloop raises $50M from Benchmark to let non-technical employees build AI agents

key_facts.fact: Gumloop raised $50 million led by Benchmark Partners to scale its platform that enables non-technical employees to build and deploy reliable AI agents that autonomously handle complex, multistep tasks without coding.
key_facts.excerpt: The company claims that it now allows teams at organizations to deploy reliable AI agents that autonomously handle complex, multistep tasks, all without ever needing to write code.

key_facts.fact: Enterprise customers include Shopify, Ramp, Gusto, Samsara, Instacart, and Opendoor, with teams using the platform to automate repetitive workflows across their organizations.
key_facts.excerpt: The company claims that it now allows teams at organizations like Shopify, Ramp, Gusto, Samsara, Instacart, and Opendoor to deploy reliable AI agents.

key_facts.fact: Benchmark GP Everett Randle stated that 'the key to success lies in empowering every worker with AI superpowers,' positioning Gumloop's agent builder as the tool to 'unlock that potential.'
key_facts.excerpt: Randle stated that 'the key to success lies in empowering every worker with AI superpowers,' positioning Gumloop's agent builder as the tool to 'unlock that potential.'

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini Embedding 2, its first natively multimodal embedding model

key_facts.fact: Google launched Gemini Embedding 2 on March 12, its first natively multimodal embedding model that processes text, images, video, audio, and documents in a single unified system, replacing the need for separate per-modality embedding models.
key_facts.excerpt: Google launched Gemini Embedding 2, described as 'its first natively multimodal embedding model supporting text, images, video, audio, and documents for enterprise use.'

key_facts.fact: The model uses Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), enabling flexible vector dimension outputs that let developers optimize the tradeoff between performance and cost without retraining.
key_facts.excerpt: The model employs Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), enabling flexible vector dimension outputs. This approach allows developers to optimize performance and cost based on specific use cases without retraining.

key_facts.fact: Gemini Embedding 2 consolidates text, image, video, and audio processing into one architecture, streamlining enterprise AI workflows that previously required maintaining separate embedding models for different content types.
key_facts.excerpt: Rather than maintaining separate models for different content types, Gemini Embedding 2 consolidates text, image, video, and audio processing into one architecture, streamlining enterprise AI workflows.

sources.title: Gemini Embedding 2 Unifies Text, Images, Video in One Model
